svg.title: Four statements, one fetch
svg.desc: Four parties each state one bound on a memory fetch: software states the bytes it needs and in what order, the operating system states how far they stay physically contiguous, the DRAM controller states where the row ends, and the cache promises room for the bytes until they are used. The fetch is the smallest of the four bounds.
svg.text: HOLD THIS UNTIL I ASK · WHAT THE CONTRACT SHOULD SAY
Each party states the fact it owns. Nothing is predicted: the fetch is computed from the statements, and it is the smallest of the four.
“These bytes, in this order, over this much program progress.”
“The row that contains them ends here.”
“Room for this many bytes. Held until they are used.”
bytes ahead of the current access →
fetched, as one batch, inside one row open
Three facts and one promise. The promise is the cache’s, about its own state, and it is what turns the fetch into a hold.
None of the four mentions time. If the fetch is ever wrong, a statement was false, and a false statement has an owner.
